summary: Extends the Next Hop Resolution Protocol so it can find next hops for private addresses used in a virtual private network on a shared non-broadcast network. It is a standards-track document at the proposed standard level.

eli5.summary: It is a helper that finds the shortcut between two private offices over a shared network, even when their addresses are private.

questions: next hop resolution protocol for private addresses
what is a vpn-aware nhrp entity
what is the nhrp device capabilities extension
subtitle: Teaching NHRP to find shortcuts for private VPN addresses that may overlap with other networks.

tldr.problem: NHRP assumes addresses belong to the public address space, but VPNs use private addresses that can overlap with other VPNs or the public Internet, so an address only has meaning inside its own VPN.
tldr.mechanism: A VPN-aware NHRP device marks its traffic with a VPN identifier, either through a VPN-specific LLC/SNAP header or through VPN signalling, and uses a new Device Capabilities extension so peers learn who is VPN-aware.
tldr.outcome: NHRP can resolve private VPN addresses on a shared NBMA network and still work alongside legacy NHRP devices that know nothing about VPNs.

today: RFC 2735 is a Proposed Standard published in December 1999, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the NHRP of RFC 2332.

sections.title: Why NHRP Needs VPN Support
sections.content:
The NBMA Next Hop Resolution Protocol (NHRP) finds the NBMA subnetwork address of the NBMA next hop toward a public internetworking layer address. The original specification has an implicit understanding that a control message applies to the public address space.

A key feature of a Virtual Private Network (VPN) service is the use of a private address space that may overlap with another VPN or the public Internet. Such an address has meaning only inside its own VPN, so the VPN that gives the address meaning, its scope, must be identified. This RFC describes the enhancements that let NHRP resolve private VPN addresses on a shared NBMA network.

It also covers a practical issue: legacy NHRP devices that are not VPN-aware may need to be used within the same service.
sections.eli5: If two companies both have a Room 12, you must say which company you mean. This RFC teaches the address helper to ask which one.

sections.title: VPN-Aware and Non-VPN-Aware Entities
sections.content:
The RFC defines a VPN-aware NHRP entity as one that implements these enhancements, and a non-VPN-aware entity as one deployed inside a single VPN without knowing about VPNs. NHRP devices as specified in the original NHRP RFC are examples of the latter. The Default Routing Instance is the context used when a packet carries no VPN indication; it may be the public Internet or a particular VPN.

A VPN-aware entity may take part in more than one VPN. A non-VPN-aware entity belongs to exactly one VPN without being aware of it, so a VPN-aware entity talking to it must be configured, by administrative means outside this document, to associate the right VPN-ID with what it receives.

VPN-aware entities must only send a non-VPN-aware entity information from that entity's own VPN, and must not include any VPN-ID indication in what they send it.
sections.eli5: Some helpers know about different buildings and some only know their own. The smart helpers must be told which building each simple helper lives in, and must never tell one building's secrets to another.

sections.title: Indicating the VPN
sections.content:
A VPN-aware device forwarding a packet for a VPN must indicate the VPN in one of two ways: explicitly, using a VPN-specific LLC/SNAP header, or implicitly, through VPN signalling on the control path. This applies to control messages between clients and servers as well as shortcut traffic between clients. A device using VPN signalling should not also indicate the VPN-ID explicitly on that path.

The RFC chose a header rather than an NHRP extension. Transit NHRP servers are not required to process extensions, so already-deployed servers might resolve the request in the public address space and cause routing problems. A prepended LLC/SNAP header can also be used on both control and data paths. A server passing a message on may change the format of the VPN indication but must keep the same VPN-ID.

A message that arrives from a VPN-aware device with no VPN indication applies to the default routing instance.
sections.eli5: You can either write the building name on every envelope, or send the mail through a pipe that only goes to one building. Either way, the building has to be clear.

sections.title: The Device Capabilities Extension
sections.content:
To learn whether a partner is VPN-aware, the RFC adds the NHRP Device Capabilities extension. A VPN-aware source MUST attach it to every Resolution Request. It SHOULD set the Source Capabilities field to show VPN support. The compulsory bit MUST be zero, so a non-VPN-aware server can safely ignore it, and the A-bit SHOULD be set to ask only for authoritative answers, to avoid replies from non-VPN-aware servers.

An egress server that receives the extension replies with the Target Capabilities flag showing whether the destination is VPN-aware. Without the extension, or if the source is non-VPN-aware, the egress server MAY reject the request (the default), accept it if the destination is also non-VPN-aware, offer itself as the destination using its own NBMA address, or accept it if the VPN-ID identifies the destination's default routing instance.

Network administrators MUST avoid configurations where a VPN-aware client is authoritatively served by a non-VPN-aware server. The extension SHOULD NOT be included in Register Request and Reply messages.
sections.eli5: Before talking, each helper says whether it understands buildings. If the other side does not, they either politely refuse or take the message themselves.

sections.title: Packet Formats
sections.content:
The VPN encapsulation header begins with the LLC/SNAP indication 0xAA-AA-03, then the IANA OUI 0x00-00-5E and the IANA-allocated PID 0x00-08 for VPN encapsulation. A PAD byte (0x00, ignored on receipt) keeps it 32-bit aligned. Then come the VPN-related OUI and the VPN Index, both defined in RFC 2685. The remainder of the PDU keeps its normal LLC/SNAP format.

The Device Capabilities extension has Type 0x0009 and Length 0x0008. Its compulsory bit is 0. It carries a Source Capabilities word and a Target Capabilities word, and in each the lowest bit, the V bit, is 1 when the device is VPN-aware and 0 when it is not. Unused bits must be zero when sent and ignored on receipt.
sections.eli5: The VPN label is a small tag stuck on the front of each message, followed by the normal message. The capabilities note is a yes-or-no box saying whether the sender understands buildings.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.content:
Two new NHRP error codes are defined: 16 (VPN mismatch), returned when a packet's VPN-ID conflicts with one set earlier, for example by signalling, and 17 (VPN not supported), returned when a device receives a message for a VPN it does not support. If a VPN-aware server cannot find a route for a VPN message, it SHOULD return the existing code 6 (protocol address unreachable).

In each case the entity MAY instead silently drop the packet to avoid certain security issues. Error indications must carry the offending VPN-ID by encapsulation or signalling, except when sent to a non-VPN-aware device.
sections.eli5: If a message names the wrong building, or a building the helper does not serve, the helper says so. Sometimes it stays quiet instead, so strangers cannot learn anything.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
For any VPN, information must not be misdirected to other VPNs or be accessible while crossing a shared infrastructure. The RFC therefore RECOMMENDS using these VPN functions together with NHRP authentication. Where an entity does not trust all NHRP entities, or is unsure end-to-end authentication is available, it may use IPsec.

For IANA, the LLC/SNAP protocol ID 0x00-08 was already allocated in conjunction with RFC 2684, and no further IDs are needed. IANA is the owner of the VPN-related OUI 0x00-00-5E and may itself allocate VPN indices; using those indices here is reserved and requires allocation and approval by the IESG.
sections.eli5: Mixing up buildings would leak private mail, so the helpers should check ID cards. For extra safety the mail itself can be locked in a box.

fields.name: PID
fields.desc: Allocated by IANA for VPN encapsulation.

fields.name: PAD
fields.desc: Coded 0x00 for 32-bit alignment; ignored on receipt.

fields.name: VPN Index
fields.desc: Identifies the VPN within that OUI.
